stepExplanation:
Using g = GM/r² for gravitational acceleration:
$$g = \frac{GM}{r^2} = \frac{(6.67 \times 10^{-11})(6.0 \times 10^{24})}{(6.8 \times 10^6)^2}$$
$$g = \frac{4.0 \times 10^{14}}{4.62 \times 10^{13}} = 8.65 \text{ m/s}^2$$
stepBody: Use g = GM/r² to calculate the gravitational acceleration at this altitude. Give your answer in m/s² (to 2 decimal places).
